paragraph_audit.reason: Section 1.2 describes model, Input, and Output operation but creates no operative grant or duty.
Section 1.3 contains a provider notice commitment conditioned on a change that may greatly affect user rights.
Section 1.4 states a provider commitment to take cybersecurity and stable-operation measures.
Section 1.5 is an availability warranty disclaimer and says features may vary by jurisdiction.
Section 1.6 describes link visibility and scraping risks and recommends precautions without imposing them as mandatory duties.
Section 2.1 conditions underage users' service use on legal-guardian consent; the provider's protective-measures statement is not modeled as a user activity rule.
Section 2.2 requires registration, specified information, and agreement before service use; account non-transferability is also captured.
Section 2.3 introduces the commitments itemized in the following lines.
The four separately stated account commitments in lines 259–262 are represented.
Section 2.4's credential safeguarding, secure logout, and conditional immediate-notice duties are extracted; account recovery is described as an available procedure.
Section 2.5 gives the user an option to discontinue use, terminate, and delete the account, subject to agreed conditions.
Both post-deletion provider rights and their distinct legal-retention and pre-deletion-misconduct conditions are represented.
Section 3.1's use grant and the cumulative requirements for publishing or disseminating outputs are represented.
Section 3.2's alternative prohibited uses and purposes are represented.
Section 3.3 grants DeepSeek a technical user-behavior review right for legal and compliance requirements.
Section 3.4 introduces the operative prohibition on generating, expressing, or promoting the listed categories.
Section 3.4(1)'s alternative content characteristics are extracted.
Section 3.4(2)'s provoking, antagonizing, bullying, and trolling categories are extracted.
Section 3.4(3)'s possible effects on another are extracted as alternative triggers.
Section 3.4(4)'s discrimination prohibition and illustrative grounds are extracted.
